rgb: This is a downward-looking, top-down egocentric view of an outdoor garden bed containing leafy green plants and brown soil immediately ahead of and beneath the seated or squatting camera wearer; no other people appear. The wearer’s bent knees and bare lower legs are partially visible along the frame’s bottom edge, approximately 0.3 to 0.4 metres from the camera, and a thick area of leafy greens spans the upper two-thirds of the image from about 0.5 to 1.2 metres ahead. On the soil directly before the legs and easily reachable by hand, roughly 0.5 to 0.6 metres from the camera, are a curved metal sickle blade at the centre and, to its right, a small round metal dish filled with plant clippings; the two objects are separated by around 0.15 to 0.2 metres. During frames 1 and 2, the wearer’s left hand grips a bundle of green stems at bottom-centre, about 0.4 metres away, as the right hand works immediately beside it and partly blocks the bundle and underlying soil. In frame 3, the right hand travels approximately 0.2 metres rightward, hovering directly over and partially obscuring the metal dish, then returns to the stem bundle in frame 4, when the right arm and hand once more hide most of the dish. By frame 5, the viewpoint pans slightly upward and left toward the plants, moving the right hand and metal dish beyond the bottom-right boundary while the left knee, the left hand holding the bundle, and part of the sickle blade remain visible at the bottom right.
depth: The monocular depth visualization shows a top-down egocentric perspective of the camera wearer squatting on the ground and looking downward toward leafy green plants. No other people are present, and nobody is looking at the camera. At the lower edge, the wearer’s bent left and right knees form the closest surfaces at about 0.3 to 0.4 metres. Their left and right hands, spaced approximately 0.1 to 0.3 metres apart, extend forward at 0.4 to 0.5 metres over soil located around 0.6 to 0.8 metres away; a curved sickle blade and a small metal bowl to the right are nearby, and everything is within arm’s reach. Through frames 1–4, the right hand travels from the harvested bundle at bottom-centre to the metal bowl on the right and then back again. In frame 5, the camera tilts a little upward and left, causing the right knee and bowl to move mostly outside the view, while the left hand partly covers the sickle and the soil underneath. Relative to the RGB strip, this map distinctly separates the height layers of the individual upper leaves, shown brighter at roughly 0.4 to 0.5 metres, from the lower foliage and recessed soil below, which merge in colour and shadow. Still, its depth estimates are unreliable: bright near-depth values are assigned to sunlit upper leaves in the upper half, making them seem as close as the wearer’s knees at about 0.3 to 0.4 metres, whereas shaded soil pockets in frames 3 and 4 become pitch-black infinite depth.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation display extracts only foreground items along the bottom of this downward-facing scene—namely the camera wearer’s limbs and the small metal container—and leaves the complete upper garden bed, including its leafy plants, soil, and sickle, unlabelled and black. Along the bottom edge, about 0.3 to 0.6 metres from the head-mounted camera and within arm’s reach, the wearer’s left knee/leg and left arm appear on the left, while the right hand/leg appear on the right; these parts are roughly 0.1 to 0.3 metres apart. The container, classified as a 'bowl' in frames 1–2 but as a 'cup' in frame 3, sits immediately above and in front of the right leg at approximately 0.6 metres, and no other people are present. Over the five frames, the right-side 'person' mask moves right into the bowl in frame 3, partly covering the container, and shifts back toward the centre in frame 4. Every mask vanishes entirely in frame 5 after the camera tilts upward and left, although portions of the lower limbs remain visible at the bottom border. In frames 1–3, segmentation clarifies the precise border between the wearer’s skin and the neighbouring metal bowl, an area that looks somewhat cluttered among the soil and chopped greens in the RGB view. Even so, the result is highly unreliable: it divides the one camera wearer into two or three separate 'person' instances, separating the left leg/arm from the right arm/leg; changes the bowl’s category to 'cup' in frame 3; omits the occluded bowl in frame 4; and detects no body parts or objects whatsoever in frame 5.
pose: Across all five frames, the body-and-hand skeleton visualization is almost completely black. It finds no yellow body skeleton for the downward-looking camera wearer, whose head and torso lie outside the view behind the camera, and confirms that no additional people are present or facing the wearer. The only output is one magenta 2D hand skeleton representing the wearer’s right hand within arm’s reach, around 0.4 to 0.5 metres from the camera; it appears in the lower-centre of frame 2 and the lower-right portion of frame 3. From frame 2 to frame 3, this detected right hand moves about 0.2 metres rightward and slightly upward to reach inside the metal bowl, which is roughly 0.6 metres from the camera and about 0.2 metres to the right of the left hand. Its fingers point downward and leftward, and the detection then disappears in frames 4 and 5 as the camera turns slightly upward. When visible in frames 2 and 3, the magenta wireframe exposes the exact articulation and bending of the right thumb and fingers, including where they overlap and self-occlude against the plant stems and bowl rim in the RGB image. Nonetheless, the pose result is mostly unreliable: it entirely fails to detect the wearer’s visible left hand holding the greens in every one of the five frames, does not find the right hand in frames 1, 4, or 5, and never tracks the visible lower legs along the bottom boundary.
